questions.stem: Which of the following describes the pathogenesis of gastrointestinal symptoms in Parkinson’s disease?
questions.stemHtml: Which of the following describes the pathogenesis of gastrointestinal symptoms in Parkinson’s disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Accumulation of Lewy bodies in the neurons of the enteric nervous systems

options.label: B
options.text: Accumulation of alpha-synuclein in the mucosa of the gastrointestinal tract

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: Side effect of levodopa preparations used in the treatment of Parkinson’s disease

questions.answerText: Accumulation of alpha-synuclein in the mucosa of the gastrointestinal tract
questions.solution: Correct Option B - Accumulation of alpha-synuclein in the mucosa of the gastrointestinal tract: Studies have shown that on biopsy, patients with Parkinson’s disease have deposition alpha-synuclein aggregates, a key component of Lewy bodies, in the mucosa of their entire GI tract. The concentration of aggregates decreases down the GI tract and is highest in the submandibular salivary glands. However, this does not entirely correlate with symptoms: although the colon and rectum have the lowest concentration of aggregates, constipation and defecatory dysfunction are the earliest and most common GI manifestations seen in Parkinson’s disease. It is unknown whether there is Lewy body accumulation in the enteric nervous system. There is no atrophy of the smooth muscle (that has been documented thus far) in the GI tract. Finally, levodopa preparations are not known to impact GI motility in patients. Incorrect Options: Option A - Accumulation of Lewy bodies in the neurons of the enteric nervous system: This statement is not accurate. While Lewy bodies, which are abnormal protein aggregates primarily composed of alpha-synuclein, are a hallmark of Parkinson's disease, they tend to accumulate in the central nervous system (CNS), particularly in neurons of the substantia nigra, which is part of the brain. They are less commonly associated with the enteric nervous system, which controls the gastrointestinal tract. However, the presence of Lewy bodies in the enteric nervous system can contribute to gastrointestinal symptoms in Parkinson's disease. Option C - Atrophy of longitudinal smooth muscles along the gastrointestinal tract secondary to denervation of these muscles: This statement is not entirely accurate. While Parkinson's disease can lead to degeneration of neurons in the enteric nervous system, which can impact the functioning of smooth muscles in the gastrointestinal tract, the denervation primarily affects the myenteric plexus, which controls the contraction of circular muscles. Longitudinal muscles are less affected by denervation in Parkinson's disease. Additionally, the primary issue related to gastrointestinal symptoms in Parkinson's disease is the accumulation of alpha-synuclein, as mentioned in the correct option. Option D - Side effect of levodopa preparations used in the treatment of Parkinson’s disease: While levodopa is a common medication used to manage the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease, including tremors and rigidity, it is not directly related to the pathogenesis of gastrointestinal symptoms. questions.solution: Correct Option D - Gastric electrical stimulation is not associated with a significant reduction in abdominal pain in patients with gastroparesis: The gastric electrical neurostimulator, sold as the Enterra Therapy system, is only FDA-approved for humanitarian use due to probable benefit for the treatment of refractory diabetic and idiopathic gastroparesis. Potential candidates are those with refractory severe nausea and vomiting who have failed optimal antiemetic and prokinetic drug therapy for at least a year. Most studies have shown no benefit of gastric stimulation in the reduction of abdominal pain. Incorrect Options: Option A - Intrapyloric injection of botulinum toxin has been shown in randomized trials to be superior to placebo for treatment of this condition: Intrapyloric injection of botulinum toxin is not recommended for the treatment of diabetic gastroparesis. Option C - Gastric electrical stimulation works by gastric electrical pacing alone: Gastric electrical stimulation consists primarily of high-frequency gastric electrical stimulation and gastric electrical pacing. Early testing and treatment of celiac disease in this population is key since it can be associated with severe neuropathy, ataxia, and retinopathy in this population. Main duct IPMNs have a higher malignant potential, and resection is recommended. Side-branch IPMNs have a lower malignant potential; still, resection is recommended with any of the following factors: clinical symptoms (eg. pain, nausea, weight loss), duct diameter greater than 5 mm, cyst larger than 3 cm (not 1 cm), thick irregular wall, or nodularity. questions.solution: Correct Option C - Jackhammer esophagus: Jackhammer or hypercontractile esophagus is characterized by 2/10 test swallows with a DCI >8000 mm/s/cm. The Chicago Classification scheme of esophageal motility diagnosis categorizes motility disorders based on esophageal pressure topography studies. EGJ morphology is not a defining criteria for motility studies but can identify a hiatus hernia. A hiatus hernia can distort EPT metrics. Basal EGJ pressure is also not a defining criterion but in some disorders it can be pertinent, including GERD and achalasia. Type I EGJ is normal. IRP is based on the median value of 10 test swallows and is a major diagnostic criterion for achalasia and EGJ outflow obstruction. Integrated relaxation pressure measures adequacy of LES relaxation with swallowing. Abnormal IRP is consistent with esophageal motility disorders and is defined as the average minimum EGJ pressure for 4 seconds within seconds of swallowing. In patients with hypercontractile esophagus, the IRP is normal. The upper limit of normal is 15 mmHg. questions.solution: Correct Option D - Extramammary Paget's disease: This is extramammary Paget's disease. Histologically, the cells can be confused with melanoma. A negative S-100 will rule out melanoma since melanoma would have been positive for S-100. Paget's tumor cells stain positive for mucin using PAS or Alcian blue.
